masking: T2 (and the per-hop half of T3) only counts as a filter bypass once T1's initial-URL check exists; in the pinned tree no check exists at all (check.py:86 has no callers), so fixing A is what exposes B.

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T2, turning FOLLOWLOCATION off globally (http_request.py:114), breaks every hoster/CDN redirect that plugin.load relies on by default (plugin.py:164 redirect=True). Redirects to public hosts must keep working, so the fix has to check each hop.

Pinning or checking the connected socket address (the robust T6 fix) checks the proxy's address when a proxy is configured (http_request.py:171-172). That rejects a legitimate loopback/LAN proxy and never sees the real target; with SOCKS remote DNS (:163-168) local resolution is irrelevant.
A guard that rejects any non-global or hostless target would also reject the local-path container branch (container.py:57 remote=False), which must keep working for uploaded containers.

fairness_risks: Downloading from a LAN host such as a NAS at 192.168.x.x through DefaultPlugin is a plausible legitimate use that a strict non-global rule refuses; the pinned code has no allow-list or config switch for it.
A loopback/LAN proxy (http_request.py:154-177) must keep working; a test that refuses non-global connect peers would break it.
Redirects to public CDN hosts must keep working (plugin.py:164, downloader.py:185); a 'no redirects' rule contradicts normal hoster behaviour.
Local container paths (container.py:57 remote=False) and the tmp_ upload path (api/__init__.py:658-665) must not go through a network-address check.
A T6 hidden test has to fix how resolution is mocked (getaddrinfo vs curl's own resolver), so it may unfairly bind the solver to one implementation.

design.why: These are four independent groups. T2 is the advisory B route and sits in the lower network layer (M3). T4 is a deepseek-type M1 entry point in the API module with a strong reason to dismiss ('not a download'). T7 is a mimo-type shape trap: the repo's freshly added IPv4-only resolver lures solvers. T8 is a mimo-type coupled value: proxy connect peers are legitimately loopback, which punishes over-hardening. T1 must be fixed anyway because A is absent from the pinned tree. T3/T5 are alternatives to T4 but share its group: one guard at HTTPRequest.set_request_context (http_request.py:224-260), which HTTPChunk.get_handle also calls (http_chunk.py:187), closes all of T1/T3/T4/T5. T4 is the one furthest from the report. T6 is left out because a test for it is hard to make fair.

Excluded as protocol variants and not recorded as traps: non-http schemes (file://, gopher://) reaching curl with no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction (http_request.py:110-138), and XDCC's raw socket connect to the URL-supplied IRC server (XDCC.py:139) or the bot-supplied DCC IP (XDCC.py:1123, 1142). libcurl's default REDIR_PROTOCOLS depends on its version and was not checked.
